author: pmventures-aa
body:
V3 Phase 2, item 1.

## The problem

HQ had five drilldowns wearing one component. You arrived from a dashboard tile, saw one table's open rows, and left. That answers "how many open tickets are there" and refuses to answer the question people actually have, which is **"what needs me today"**.

It could not tell you which items were yours, which were late, which had nobody on them, or which had not moved in a month. It could not show a ticket next to the invoice for the same client.

## What makes it a queue

**Everything in one place.** `GET /admin/work-queue` reads seven tables in one union: cases, matters, tasks, calls, invoices, document requests and document reviews.

**A vocabulary of responsibility.** Owner already existed in every table, under two different column names (`assigned_staff_user_id`, and `staff_user_id` on calls), and was shown in almost none of them. `waiting_on` and `next_step` existed nowhere, which is why a stalled item looked identical to a moving one.

**The ability to change it from here.** Owner, waiting-on and next step are editable inline. A queue you can only read is a report.

## Schema

`0103_work_queue_attention.sql` adds `work_item_attention`, a side table keyed by `(item_type, item_id)`.

One re-runnable `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` rather than fourteen `ALTER`s. SQLite has no `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS`, which is the trap `0094`-`0097` fell into and `0098` had to rebuild; `0099`, `0101` and `0102` all solved it this way.

Owner is written to **the table's own column**, never to the side table, so assignment stays the same fact the rest of HQ already reads. Only `waiting_on` and `next_step`, which no table has, live in the side table.

## Views

Thirteen saved views, every one backed by real data with no invented destinations: My work, Due today, Overdue, Unassigned, Not moving, Waiting on client, Waiting on provider, Waiting on internal review, Calls, Cases, Document requests, Approvals, All open work.

They are applied in the browser off one request, so every count is correct and switching views costs nothing. Past the 1,000-item cap the response says so rather than quietly showing a subset.

## Compatibility

The `open-items/:type` links from the dashboard tiles still work. They are filters of the queue now instead of separate pages, and the page title still names which filter is applied.

## Verification

- `shared/workQueue.ts` typechecks and is covered by 24 new tests in `tests/workQueue.test.ts`, including the off-by-one on "due today is not overdue", stale-vs-scheduled, and per-view examples that assert every view can actually fill.
- Contract tests read the endpoint and the migration: scope check precedes any write, a patch that sets one field does not blank the other, owner goes to the base table.
- Full suite: 1419 passed. Two existing assertions were updated to the new page rather than loosened (`hqHeadings` now asserts the queue names its filter; the wide-table guarantee in `adminTablesMobile` is unchanged).

author: baldrick-h2[bot]
body:
A defect I introduced, the fix, and the cost the fix carries.

## What happened

Adding `required_status_checks` to the `deploys` ruleset at 22:02 stopped every promotion until 00:20.

A commit that has **just been created** has no check runs against it, so GitHub rejects the push with `GH013: 4 of 4 required status checks are expected`. Dropping the `pull_request` rule — which open question Q3 did deliberately, so promotion would keep working — does not help. The two rules block a direct push independently.

Ten promotions failed: six from `servitium`, four from `plepic`. Nothing was down, because the `live` overlays kept serving the digests promoted at 21:47, but nothing shipped either.

**Why it went unnoticed:** the pull request checks were green, and those are what I read. The failure is in the `Release` workflow that runs *after* the merge. Four promotions had already failed before the batch that finally exposed it.

## The fix

Both deployer apps are bypass actors on the `deploys` ruleset — `servitium-deployer` (4345014) and `plepic-deployer` (4614643), `bypass_mode: always` because the push is direct, not through a pull request.

Verified rather than assumed: both promotions re-run and landed. `deploys/main` now carries `a775743` from `servitium-deployer` and `7386c6c` from `plepic-deployer`, and each `live` digest matches its repository's current `main`.

## The cost, written down

A bypass actor is exempt from the **whole ruleset**, not from one rule. Both apps can now also delete and force-push `deploys/main`. Accepted because each pushes a single fast-forward commit from a workflow reviewed like any other file, and the alternative is no status checks on `deploys` at all.

## Two corrections

`security.md` said the required contexts were `Validate`. They are `Manifests`, `Shell`, `Workflows`, `Documentation`.

`security.md` also now states the general rule and how to check it: watch the post-merge run, not the pull request.

## Routed to `plepic`

It has no release-failure notification. `servitium`'s `notify.yml` fires on `workflow_run` and posts an `@mention` on any non-success conclusion, so its six failures were announced six times. `plepic`'s four were silent. Recorded as the top item in the handoff's routed-work list.

body:
Documentation only — `CLAUDE.md`, +147 lines, no code and no migration.

Written so a fresh session doesn't rediscover tonight's problems the hard way.

## New sections

**Custom order quotes: the customer is the weak link, not the code.** The quote pipeline works; the last metre doesn't. The approval UI exists only on the Track page, only with the order token in the URL — so the sole thing that can bring a customer there is a web push, and FCM's `ok: true / status: 200` means *FCM accepted the message*, not that anyone saw it. Guest tokens live only in `orders.push_token`, so nothing tracks their health and nothing can ever mark them dead.

Order #1795 is written up as the worked example: quote #15 issued 23:28, reminder 23:42, expired unanswered 23:43, quote #16 at 00:00 — **four** pushes all accepted by FCM, **zero** `view` calls all evening. #1739 the same night, same story. Includes the diagnostic (check for `view` calls before blaming the code) and the correct way to approve on a customer's behalf, through `accept_custom_order_quote` rather than by writing money columns.

**Rate limits: size them by how the caller behaves.** The bug that hid the confirm button, stated generally: a button-press limit applied to a polled read. 10 per 10 minutes against a 10-second poll saturates in ~100 seconds and, on a 10-minute window, never drains. Records that the *window* matters as much as the number — `customer-order-access` polls just as hard and survives because its window is 1 minute — and flags `driver-self-service` as still running on 1.5× headroom.

**Closing an order by hand.** `admin_force_delivered` credits the newest `Offered` assignment, so an order nobody accepted still moves cash onto a driver who never took it. Documents the `is_admin()` claim approach (set the JWT so it runs as the designed path and the event log gets a real actor, rather than writing rows around the guard), that the cash delta must be asserted before commit, and that `driver_flat_earning_egp` being `0` books every forced delivery at zero driver earning.

## Extended sections

- **CI** — `yaml.safe_load` passing is not proof a workflow is valid; PyYAML accepts duplicate keys silently. A failed run with zero jobs and `created_at == updated_at` means an invalid workflow file, not a failed build. Also notes edge functions are deployed by hand and `check:drift` still cannot run.
- **Verifying anything RLS-related** — RLS enabled with *zero policies* is deliberate on `order_quotes`; don't "fix" it by adding a policy.
- **Working rules** — the sandbox cannot reach `app.gosalka.com` or `supabase.co`; verify deploys by matching content-derived asset hashes against the wrangler upload list, and reach production through the MCP servers.
- **Things not to touch** — order #1795 added, with why it was closed by hand and that its quote's `accepted_by` is null because it was a phone approval.

author: lukislp
body:
## Summary
Root cause of the pan-zoom feature never working (#27, #28, #29 all shipped, none fixed it) - found via a live browser DevTools investigation: **Material for MkDocs renders each Mermaid diagram into a closed shadow root** attached to the \`.mermaid\` host element. That's unreachable from any outside code by design:
- \`querySelectorAll(".mermaid svg")\` never matches
- A \`MutationObserver\` on \`document.body\` never sees the insertion
- \`host.attachShadow()\` itself throws \`NotSupportedError\` once Material has already attached its own closed root

\`svg-pan-zoom\` needs a direct \`<svg>\` reference, so it fundamentally cannot work here - confirmed live (the library itself works fine on a plain light-DOM SVG, it just never gets one). CDN blocking, stale caching, and Mermaid's own async rendering (all investigated and "fixed" over the past several iterations) were red herrings - none of it mattered once the target element was unreachable in the first place.

**New approach**: never look inside the host. Treat it as an opaque box and pan/zoom it via a CSS \`transform\`, the same way you'd zoom a photo - whatever's inside (shadow DOM or not) comes along for the ride. Wraps each host in a fixed-height, \`overflow: hidden\` viewport with a +/-/reset button overlay; drag and scroll-wheel adjust \`translate()\`/\`scale()\` on the host itself. Detects "Mermaid has actually rendered something" by polling the host's own rendered height instead of querying its content (shadow DOM content still affects normal layout from the outside, it's just not queryable) - same defensive design as before: if the JS never gets the chance to run, the diagram falls back to its plain, always-fully-visible static size.

# Spec Conformance Checklist

**Linked Spec Issue**: #1860

Fixes #1860

## Problem

`OperationExecutor` kept every operation run in memory forever, and each run
appended one dictionary for every log record the operation emitted. The portal
runs as one long-lived Gunicorn worker with `--workers 1`, so the memory only
rose until an out-of-memory kill interrupted a write to the data directory.

## What changed

- `log_messages` and `debug_messages` are now a `collections.deque` with a
  `maxlen`. The deque drops the oldest entry, so one high-volume run cannot
  fill the worker memory.
- `dropped_log_count` counts every entry a cap discarded. `_run_to_dict` and
  `_run_to_summary` report the count, so the operator sees the truncation.
- `OperationExecutor._prune_runs` keeps the most recent finished runs and drops
  the rest. It also drops a finished run that passed the retention period. It
  follows the `PortalEventBus._cleanup_stale_subscribers` pattern.
- `_select_stale_runs` reads the finished runs only, so a pending run and a
  running run are never evicted.
- `_configure_limits` reads `PORTAL_RUN_LOG_MAX_ENTRIES` (default 2000),
  `PORTAL_RUN_HISTORY_MAX` (default 50) and `PORTAL_RUN_RETENTION_SECONDS`
  (default 3600). An unusable value falls back to the default and logs a
  warning.
- `deploy/.env.example` documents all three settings in a short section placed
  immediately after the `WEB_PORT` line.

The read boundary already copied each store into a list, so the JSON response
shape does not change apart from the new `dropped_log_count` field.

body:
## Summary

This PR adds the `animica` namespace with CAIP-2, CAIP-10, and CAIP-19 profiles.

[Animica](https://animica.org) is a live proof-of-work Layer 1 whose accounts sign with post-quantum ML-DSA-65 (FIPS 204) signatures and whose smart contracts run in a Python VM. Mainnet has been running since 2026-04-06 (chain id `1`, genesis `0xa0892158cf997c56e91d0aa12e60c36037dae34800a2b54111a8fa17ec88b7de`). The native token ANM has 9 decimals.

## Motivation

The identifier `animica:1` is already in production use today: Animica's [x402](https://github.com/x402-foundation/x402) ANM settlement lane uses it as its network id, as do its MCP tooling and chain parameters. This is the same situation as the `bsv` (#190) and `kaspa` (#193) submissions, where a payment protocol was already exchanging a CAIP-2 identifier and the namespace registration documents it. Wallets and dapps integrating Animica need CAIP-2/10/19 identifiers they can rely on rather than each inventing their own.

Animica cannot live in `eip155`: it is not an EVM chain, its addresses are bech32m strings carrying a signature-scheme id and a SHA3-256 key digest, its transactions are canonical CBOR signed with ML-DSA-65, and its chain id `1` would collide with Ethereum mainnet.

## What each document defines

- **`animica/README.md`** - namespace overview, why it is not `eip155`, governance, and a resources list (website, explorer, public RPC, source, PyPI, normative HD-derivation doc, exchange listing).
- **`animica/caip2.md`** - `animica:<chainId>`; reference is the canonical decimal of the node's `uint32` chain id (`^(0|[1-9][0-9]{0,9})$`, bounded to `uint32`, `0` unassigned). Resolution via `chain.getChainId`, and a genesis-hash cross-check via `chain.getChainIdentity` (live response included) so a future chain reusing the id cannot be mistaken for mainnet. Valid/invalid test tables. `animica:2` (testnet) and `animica:1337` (devnet) are noted as reserved; only mainnet is public today.
- **`animica/caip10.md`** - `animica:1:anim1...`; the native address is bech32m (BIP-350, HRP `anim`, constant `0x2bc830a3`) over a 34-byte payload `u16be(alg_id) || SHA3-256(pubkey)`. Always 66 characters; ML-DSA-65 accounts (`0x1003`) start `anim1zqp`, contract addresses (`0x0000`) start `anim1qqq`. Lowercase is canonical. Regex `^anim1[02-9ac-hj-np-z]{61}$` plus checksum/length/alg-range validation. Test vectors are the three real addresses from the BIP-39 reference mnemonic in the normative HD derivation document, plus negatives (mixed case, uppercase, plain-bech32 checksum of the same payload, corrupted checksum, bare hex digest).
- **`animica/caip19.md`** - native asset `animica:1/slip44:4279885` (coin type `0x414E4D` = ASCII `ANM`, 9 decimals). SLIP-44 registration is **pending** (a PR to satoshilabs/slips is being filed alongside this one). Contract-issued tokens are explicitly reserved for a future revision rather than specified loosely.

## How it was verified

- Frontmatter of all four files parsed with PyYAML; every `[Name][]` alias resolves and none is unused; no inline external links; one sentence per line.
- Every CAIP-10 test vector was re-derived independently in Python: `SHA3-256(pubkey)` matches the published digest, bech32m encoding of `0x1003 || digest` reproduces each address byte-for-byte, each decodes with the bech32m constant to a 34-byte payload with `alg_id = 0x1003`, and each matches the regex. Each negative vector fails for exactly the stated reason (the plain-bech32 variant verifies under constant `1` and fails under `0x2bc830a3`).
- Every CAIP-2 and CAIP-19 valid/invalid identifier was checked against the profile regexes and the `uint32` bound.
- The `chain.getChainId`, `chain.getChainIdentity`, and `state.getAccount` responses shown in the profiles were captured live from `https://rpc.animica.org/rpc` on 2026-08-22.
- `bundle exec jekyll build` was not run: Ruby/Bundler are not available in the authoring environment. The pages use only the same frontmatter keys as the existing `neo`, `bsv`, and `stellar` profiles, and the site auto-discovers the `animica/` directory.

## Links

- Website: https://animica.org
- Explorer: https://explorer.animica.org
- Public RPC: `POST https://rpc.animica.org/rpc`
- Source: https://github.com/animicaorg/all
- PyPI: https://pypi.org/project/animica/
- HD derivation (normative, with the address test vectors): https://github.com/animicaorg/all/blob/36f995f241cd3e54f66c7a5a6f373d4587bbc60d/docs/wallet/HD_DERIVATION.md
- ANM trades on NonKYC: https://nonkyc.io/market/ANM_USDT

HD path: `m/44'/4279885'/account'/0'/address_index'` (all hardened, SLIP-0010 ed25519-family derivation; the final 32-byte key is the ML-DSA-65 seed).

## Known limitations

- The SLIP-44 coin type `4279885` is not yet in the registry; the CAIP-19 profile says so.
- Contract-token asset references are deliberately out of scope for this revision.
- `discussions-to` points at this PR, following the precedent of `bsv`, `stellar`, and `xync`.

# Spec Conformance Checklist

**Linked Spec Issue**: #1863

Fixes #1863

## What changed

The `/health` endpoint returned the fixed text `healthy` on every call. It never tested write
access to the data directory, which is the one resource with a documented failure. A portal that
could not write a single output file still reported a good state, so no monitor saw the fault. The
container also defined no health probe, so `Restart=always` never fired.

- **`/health` is now a liveness probe.** It reports the process state and the uptime. It reads no
  disk and it opens no network connection, so a blocked resource cannot slow the reply down. The
  body keeps the word `healthy`, so the existing monitor in `tests/e2e/test_portal_smoke.py` still
  matches.
- **`/ready` is a new readiness probe.** It writes one temporary file in the data directory and
  deletes the file again. Only a real write proves the mount is writable.
- **`/ready` also tests the SQLite database and the Mist API session.** It opens the database
  read-only when the file exists and runs one trivial query. It reads the session cloud host from
  the stored object, so it makes no network call to Mist.
- **`/ready` returns code 503 when a check fails.** The body names each failed check under
  `failed_checks`, and it carries a detail line for each check, so the operator learns how to repair
  the resource.
- **`deploy/misthelper.container` now defines a health command.** `HealthCmd=` calls `/ready`, with
  `HealthInterval=30s`, `HealthTimeout=5s`, `HealthRetries=3`, `HealthStartPeriod=20s`, and
  `HealthOnFailure=restart`. A comment states that the OCI image format rejects the `HEALTHCHECK`
  instruction, which is the reason Quadlet supplies the probe.

## Acceptance criteria from issue #1863

- [x] `/ready` returns code 503 when the data directory is not writable.
- [x] `/ready` names the failed check in the response body.
- [x] `/health` stays cheap and reports process liveness only.

      cannot carry one.
- [ ] The `misthelper` service in `compose.yml` defines a health check. **Deferred.** See the
      checklist below.
- [x] A unit test asserts `/ready` returns 503 when the data directory is read-only.

## Deferred container work

Open pull request #1825 owns the `Containerfile`, the `Dockerfile`, and `compose.yml`.
`gh pr view 1825 --json state` reports `OPEN`, so this pull request leaves all three files untouched
to avoid a merge conflict. The exact remaining change:

- [ ] `compose.yml`, the `misthelper` service near lines 4 to 57: add a `healthcheck` block that
      runs `curl --fail --silent --show-error http://localhost:8055/ready`, with `interval: 30s`,
      `timeout: 5s`, `retries: 3`, and `start_period: 20s`. This matches the pattern the ArangoDB
      service at line 84 and the Redis service at line 105 already use.
- [ ] `Containerfile`, line 113: replace the comment
      `# Note: HEALTHCHECK removed for OCI/Podman compatibility` with a comment that names
      `deploy/misthelper.container` as the location of the probe. Restore a `HEALTHCHECK`
      instruction against `/ready` only when the build switches to the Docker image format.
- [ ] `Dockerfile`, line 109: apply the same change. The Docker image format accepts `HEALTHCHECK`,
      so this file can carry
      `HEALTHCHECK --interval=30s --timeout=5s --retries=3 --start-period=20s CMD curl --fail --silent http://localhost:8055/ready || exit 1`.
- [ ] Confirm the image carries `curl` before any probe lands. A missing `curl` makes every probe
      fail and marks a good container unhealthy.

## Test results

`tests/unit/web_portal/test_dashboard_readiness.py` is a new module with 14 cases. All 14 pass.
13 of the 14 fail against the code before this change, which proves the tests hold the defect.

```
collected 25 items
tests\unit\web_portal\test_dashboard_readiness.py ..............   [ 56%]
tests\unit\web_portal\test_operation_run_registry_caps.py ...........  [100%]
25 passed in 0.94s
```

The second module arrived on `main` in pull request #1867. Both modules pass together after the
rebase.

The first run of the `pytest (coverage gate)` job failed. Coverage was not the cause. The total
reached 92.33 percent against the 80 percent floor. One case failed:
`test_ready_returns_503_when_the_database_file_is_corrupt` expected code 503 and received code 200.

Root cause: the database check ran `SELECT 1`. SQLite answers that query from memory, so it never
reads a page and it never validates the file header. A corrupt database therefore passed the check

The branch then showed no checks at all, because pull request #1867 merged first and made this

body:
Fixes #880. The [investigation is in the issue](https://github.com/BinaryBourbon/fountain/issues/880#issuecomment-5383256458); the short version is that this was never a Sprites platform bug.

## The bug

Sprites frames a finished command as stream id `3` followed by a **one-byte** exit code. Our pinned fork decoded 32 bits:

```elixir
def decode(<<@exit_id, code::big-unsigned-32>>), do: {:exit, code}
```

A 1-byte payload cannot match, so every exit frame fell through to `decode(data), do: {:unknown, data}` and was dropped. The server then closed the socket, and `Sprites.Command.handle_close_frame/3` synthesised a code:

```elixir
send(owner, {:exit, %{ref: ref}, 0})
```

Running the fork's clauses against real frames:

```
wire <<3, 0>>   -> {:unknown, <<3, 0>>}
wire <<3, 42>>  -> {:unknown, <<3, 42>>}
wire <<3, 128>> -> {:unknown, <<3, 128>>}
```

That is the "533 exit codes recorded, every one of them `0`" dataset exactly. Worth stressing that the zeroes were not lossy but **invented** — Fountain never once read a Sprites process's real status, including on the runs that looked fine.

## The fix

Move the pin from `ravi-hq/sprites-ex@c2a9642` to upstream `superfly/sprites-ex` at `v0.2.0`.

The fork branched on 2026-05-04 and never picked up upstream's two fixes: `abce09c` (2026-07-31, `big-unsigned-32` -> `unsigned-8`, plus the control path's `"code"` -> `"exit_code"`, a second bug we also carried) and `00c8592` (2026-08-03, tolerates trailing/empty payloads, fixes frame draining).

Both reasons the fork existed are upstream now — the `/v1/sprites/<name>/fs/*` filesystem URLs (`filesystem.ex:581`) and the `attach_session` URL (`sprite.ex:56-57`) — so this goes back to upstream rather than carrying a patch. The `mix.exs` comment is updated to say so.

## Blast radius

`v0.2.0` also brings control-connection multiplexing (`control.ex`, `control_conn.ex`, `control_pool.ex`, and a new `client_signals` dep). It is **opt-in**: `Sprites.Client` defaults `control_mode: false` and `Fountain.Sandbox.Sprites.Client.get!/0` does not pass it, so exec keeps using one WebSocket per command as before. Worth revisiting deliberately later, not as a side effect of this.

No Fountain code changes. `Sprites.exec/4` and its `collect/4` were already correct — they faithfully report whatever the SDK hands them, which is exactly why nothing here could catch the bug.

## Test

`apps/fountain/test/fountain/sandbox/sprites/protocol_contract_test.exs` is a contract test against the **dependency's** decoding, not our code, since that is the only place the regression can live. It covers the codes a process can actually exit with (including 128, git's `fatal:`, and 255), a trailing byte, an empty payload, and asserts a non-zero exit never decodes as `:unknown`.

Verified the guard is real by reverting the decode in `deps/` and recompiling in the test env: **4 of its 5 tests fail**, including `{:exit, 704643072}` for `<<3, 42, 0, 0, 0>>`. Restored afterwards.

Full suite green: `6 doctests, 3 properties, 3640 tests, 0 failures`. `deps.unlock --unused`, `format --check-formatted`, `credo --strict` (no issues), and `dialyzer` (0 errors) all pass individually — checked separately rather than trusting the `precommit` alias's exit code.

## Expected consequences once codes are real

Both intended, both worth watching after deploy:

- `clone_https/4` will start correctly failing conversations that today limp along on an empty directory.
- Setup scripts that have been quietly failing in production will begin surfacing as failures.

## Not fixed here

`handle_close_frame/3` still synthesises `0` when the socket closes without an exit frame — now only reachable on a genuine transport failure, where it would report success. `superfly/sprites-py` raises `NetworkError` for that case instead. Upstream's Elixir SDK has not followed; worth an upstream issue rather than a local patch.

author: ahmedhafdi-maker
body:
Measurement and hardening work run on Isambard-AI (GH200, aarch64). Four phase
gates met with real numbers — and several previously published claims corrected,
which is the part worth reviewing first.

## Corrections to existing claims

**Every reported `--sheaf-probe` number was process-dependent.** `text_stalks`
derived each token's projection from `hash((seed, token))`, and `hash()` on a
`str` is salted per interpreter. Placeholder pooled AUC ranged over **0.0–1.0**
across processes at a fixed seed. Replaced with BLAKE2b; verified byte-identical
under two `PYTHONHASHSEED` values on the real 12,576-example dev set. The
negative result itself survives (learned 0.541 vs identity 0.524, under the 0.023
noise floor) — it was right even when the numbers were not reproducible.

**End-to-end is a loss, not parity.** On 500 2Wiki examples with the surface
linker at 57.2% link accuracy: CookiX **0.366** vs BM25 **0.413** vs dense
**0.400** — below both. The previously published 0.378 vs 0.386 was parity on a
2,000-example run; `CLAIMS.md` now attributes each figure to its run.

**`tracemalloc` under-reports resident memory by 2.7×.** At 10⁶ objects it says
3121 MB while the process holds **8425 MB**. Anyone sizing a deployment from the
README's old "peak MB" column would have under-provisioned threefold.

**MuSiQue's numbers are unusable and marked so.** Its chains are reconstructed as
`anchor → answer₁ → … → answerₙ`, so the gold answer is reachable by
construction; 0.998 largely confirms the loader works.

**Three places cited commands that could not reproduce their own numbers**,
including a row in `CLAIMS.md` itself.

## Gates met

- **Phase 13** — 328 req/s sustained for 2 h, 2,358,636 requests, **0 errors**;
  at 10⁶ objects memory growth **+0.0 MB**; 20 induced `SIGKILL`s with zero data
  loss (`ops/isambard/crash_inject.py` checks every *acknowledged* write).
- **Phase 14** — group-commit on an `fsync`-bound disk: **+97.7% / +131.1% /
  +534%** at 4/8/16 threads on Lustre. The roadmap's own "~3%" was measured where
  `fsync` was cheap. Without it, throughput *falls* as writers are added.
- **Phase 17** — streaming WAL replication (`catch_up()`, O(new writes) not
  O(history)), fenced leader election, and key-based sharding.
- **Phase 18** — the dense baseline finally run: **0.578 vs 0.400** oracle. A
  dense retriever does *not* beat BM25 here (0.400 vs 0.413).
- **Phase 7** — **10⁶ objects measured**: 0.897 → 1.490 ms across a 1000× graph
  increase.

## New

`cookix eval --writes`, `--sizes`, `--dense`, `--dataset {hotpotqa,musique}`;
`backend="sharded"`; multi-tenant isolation by separate database; pluggable
rate-limit store (Redis); optional OpenTelemetry; `ops/isambard/` job harness;
`docs/deployment/multi-tenant.md`.

## Entity linking on local open weights (added since this PR opened)

Phase 18's decisive measurement is *"does a model-assisted linker clear the ~70%
link accuracy that flips end-to-end from a loss to a win?"*. It previously
existed only as a hosted path needing an `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, which makes the
resulting number expensive to reproduce and dependent on a model that can change
underneath it.

`--linker open` now points at any OpenAI-compatible `/v1/chat/completions`
endpoint (vLLM, llama.cpp, Ollama) via `COOKIX_OPEN_BASE_URL` /
`COOKIX_OPEN_MODEL`, using `urllib` — no new dependency. Requests are greedy,
because a linking benchmark that moves between identical runs is not a
measurement, and a dead endpoint degrades to the surface linker rather than
aborting a 2,000-example run. `ops/isambard/serve_open_model.py` serves local
weights over that endpoint in ~130 lines.

**The measurement itself has not landed yet** — the run is queued. Three parsing
and wiring bugs were found and fixed on the way, each of which would have
produced a plausible *number* rather than an error: splitting on `"."` turned
`"1. Xawery Zulawski"` into `"1"`; a reasoning model's `analysis` channel leaked
into the reply; and `--linker open` was missing from argparse's choices so the
stage failed after loading a 13 GB checkpoint. The first two would have shown
`open ≈ surface` and supported the false conclusion "the model does not help".

## Not claimed

- **Phase 16 needs an external security review** — cannot be self-served.
- **Phase 19 is unmet** and cannot be bought with test time. One two-hour soak is
  a soak, not mileage.
- HotpotQA's chains cannot test the *typed* traversal claim; only 2Wiki can.

254 tests passing, `ruff` clean.

author: ayaangazali
body:
Follow-up to #761, which had to drop cloud from the Windows build:

> Cloud genuinely does not link on MSVC. It is the PE data-symbol problem already documented for QHexRT [...] the carrier references the op table as DATA, and MSVC resolves imported data only via `__declspec(dllimport)` on the declaration shared with the ELF/Mach-O builds. Linux gets cloud for free; Windows cannot ship it until that is fixed, so `RAC_BACKEND_CLOUD=OFF` in the preset with the reason recorded.

That diagnosis is right, and the repo already contains the remedy twice over. This applies it to cloud.

## The structure of the failure

`engines/cloud/CMakeLists.txt` compiles `rac_plugin_entry_cloud.cpp` into **both** `rac_backend_cloud` and the thin `runanywhere_cloud` carrier. The carrier's copy does `&g_cloud_stt_ops`, and that object is defined in `rac_backend_cloud`. So the carrier holds a cross-image reference to a data symbol.

Built on macOS with `RAC_STATIC_PLUGINS=OFF`, that is visible directly:

```
── librac_backend_cloud.dylib
000000000002c288 (__DATA_CONST,__const) external _g_cloud_stt_ops
── librunanywhere_cloud.dylib
                 (undefined) external _g_cloud_stt_ops (from librac_backend_cloud)
```

`__DATA_CONST` in the defining image, `undefined` in the consumer. Mach-O binds that at load time; the PE loader will not, absent an import descriptor, which is what produces `LNK2001: unresolved external symbol g_cloud_stt_ops`.

## Why this is the house fix and not an invention

`g_cloud_stt_ops` is the only engine op table in the tree declared bare:

```c
extern const rac_stt_service_ops_t g_cloud_stt_ops;          // cloud
extern RAC_ONNX_API const rac_embeddings_service_ops_t g_onnx_embeddings_ops;   // onnx
extern "C" RAC_LLAMACPP_API const rac_vlm_service_ops_t g_llamacpp_vlm_ops = {  // llamacpp
```

`engines/onnx/rac_onnx_api.h` already explains the exact case, including why it is mandatory rather than cosmetic:

> dllimport — MANDATORY for DATA symbols such as `g_onnx_{embeddings,segmentation,diarization}_ops`, because MSVC cannot fix up a cross-image data reference the way it can synthesize a function thunk.

So this adds `RAC_CLOUD_API` as a direct peer, with `RAC_CLOUD_BUILDING` set on `rac_backend_cloud` only, exactly as `RAC_ONNX_BUILDING` is set on `rac_backend_onnx` only. `cmake/plugins.cmake` applies `COMPILE_DEFINITIONS` on both the shared path (line 201, the engine target) and the `RAC_STATIC_PLUGINS` fold path (line 133, into `rac_commons`), so iOS and WASM stay correct too, where the macro expands to default visibility.

One deviation from onnx worth flagging: `rac_onnx_api.h` sits beside its sources, but `rac_cloud_api.h` goes under `include/`. The carrier target's include path is `engines/cloud/include` and the commons include dir only, so a header at the engine root would be invisible to precisely the target that needs the dllimport side. The cloud public header is consumed by three TUs, all inside `engines/cloud`, so nothing outside the engine is affected.

## Verification, and its limit

Configured and built on macOS with `-DRAC_BACKEND_CLOUD=ON -DRAC_STATIC_PLUGINS=OFF -DRAC_BUILD_SHARED=ON`: `rac_backend_cloud` and `runanywhere_cloud` both build and link, and the `nm` output above is from that build. `RAC_STATIC_PLUGINS=ON` also configures clean.

I cannot compile MSVC on this host, so I have not watched the `LNK2001` go away. That is the same limit #761 recorded for itself ("Not verifiable off-Windows: MSVC compile behavior"). What I can show is that the reference really is cross-image data, and that this is the mechanism the two engines which *do* link on MSVC use to solve it.

I deliberately left `CMakePresets.json` alone rather than flipping `RAC_BACKEND_CLOUD=ON` for Windows in the same diff. #763 is currently editing that file, and turning the backend on is the step that should be gated on a green Windows run rather than bundled with the enabling change. Happy to add it here if you would rather see the `windows-commons-release` job prove it in one go.

author: chrisonsimtian
body:
Pangolin becomes a downstream OIDC client of the IdP instead of owning its own logins, and access is decided by group membership. Advances #468; the group model is the start of the access policy work.

## The hole this closes

The Plex source runs `allow_friends: true` with the stock `default-source-enrollment` flow — **any friend on the Plex server gets an Authentik account created on first login.** Harmless while Authentik has zero applications.

The moment Pangolin becomes one, Authentik's default with no policy binding is *"any authenticated user is allowed"*. Every Plex friend would have reached every `*.lab` and `*.arr` UI behind the SSO gate. So the binding ships with the client, not after it.

## Two independent deny-by-default layers

| Layer | Decides | Closed by |
|---|---|---|
| Authentik | may you get a token for Pangolin at all | four group bindings; no group → no binding matches |
| Pangolin | which resources you reach | its resource↔role matrix, which today grants every resource to `Admin` only |

Neither relies on the other being right. A Family member can authenticate successfully today and reach nothing — deliberate, and called out in the shape so nobody expects otherwise.

## Groups

`Homelab Admins`, `Media Admins`, `Family`, `Guests` — the taxonomy Christian picked. Only the first maps to a Pangolin `Admin`; the rest exist so the resource matrix has something to bind to next.

## The access model is a file, not UI state

Authentik discovers blueprints under `/blueprints`, so groups, the OIDC provider, the application and the policy bindings are one reviewable YAML rendered by converge.

Both client credentials are generated into Secrets Manager and read by **both** ends — Authentik's blueprint via `!Env`, Pangolin's registration via `clientIdFrom`/`clientSecretFrom`. That removes the copy-the-secret-between-two-UIs step rather than documenting it.

## Checked against the running system, not assumed

- The stock `profile` scope already emits `groups` — no custom property mapping needed
- Pangolin evaluates `roleMapping` as `jmespath.search(claims, expr)`, normalising the result to role names
- Its callback is `/auth/idp/{idpId}/oidc/callback` with the id assigned at creation — so the redirect URI must be a **regex**, not a strict URL
- Every resource currently grants `Admin` only, which is what makes layer 2 closed

## Two traps avoided

**`assetsTarget` is a dedicated directory**, not `/home/podman/authentik`. The asset push ends with `chown -R podman <assetsTarget>` and the Postgres data dir is uid 999 under keep-id — pointing it at the shared parent would have broken the database as a side effect of shipping a config file.

**`ShapeValidator` now skips `assets/` trees.** Its apiVersion probe deliberately *keeps* files it cannot parse so a typo in a real shape is never silently skipped. Blueprints use `!Env`/`!Find`/`!KeyOf` tags no general parser resolves, so they tripped that net while being exactly what it is not for. Excluded before the probe rather than by weakening it.

## Reconciled, not add-only

The IdP reconciler compares live state and corrects it, for the #309 reason — an `authUrl` pointing at a stale issuer is a login loop a clean plan would hide. The client secret is excluded from the drift check because the API never reads one back; rotating it means changing Secrets Manager and deleting the IdP so converge recreates it.

## Verification

- `ValidateShapes` 46/46 · `TestEngine` **352 passed** (+6)
- `Preview --stack Core` shows the asset render to `/home/podman/authentik-blueprints`, all four podman secrets, and `reconcile identity provider 'Authentik' + its claim→role mapping`
- Actions secrets `AUTHENTIK_PANGOLIN_CLIENT_ID` / `_SECRET` set **before** deploying, rather than discovering the gap at apply as in #446 and #471

## Not in this PR

The resource↔role matrix — which resources each of Media Admins / Family / Guests actually reaches. That is the rest of the access-policy work and wants its own change. GitHub as an upstream provider is also still to come.

author: jds300
body:
The `v0.4.0` re-publish was cancelled 30 seconds in. Two runs were created in the
same second, both holding `spinui-build-<workflow>-refs/heads/main`:

```
23:52:30Z  32538423189  push               in_progress
23:52:30Z  32538422803  workflow_dispatch  cancelled
```

## The comment was right; the config did not implement it

```yaml
# A newer test push or PR revision supersedes an older one; release assembly
# is never cancelled.
cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}
```

`cancel-in-progress` is evaluated on the **incoming** run and cancels whichever
older run holds the group, whatever kind it is. Setting it false for a dispatch
only stopped a dispatch from cancelling *others* — nothing ever protected a
dispatch from *being* cancelled. Merging shortly before releasing is the normal
order, which made the collision near certain rather than unlucky.

Releases now hold a group of their own, so the two kinds cannot reach each other
in either direction. A newer push still supersedes an older one, and a second
dispatch queues behind the first rather than interrupting it mid-publish.

## Why this is worse than a lost run

The Windows job runs `gh release create`, and the Linux job uploads to that tag
afterwards. A push landing between them publishes a release carrying **no Linux
assets at all** — no AppImage, no tarball, no zsync — while the workflow reports
only that something was cancelled. v0.4.0 lost the race early enough to be
harmless. That was luck.

## Verification

The folded scalar resolves to a single valid expression:

```
spinui-build-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}-${{ (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' || github.event_name == 'release') && 'release' || 'test' }}
```

`release_quality_gate.py` pins both halves and I confirmed it fails when the
group is reverted to the shared one. Pinned because the failure is quiet: a
cancelled run looks like every other cancelled run, and nothing else would
report this coming back.

CI on this pull request cannot prove the fix, since it only ever creates
`pull_request` runs. The honest test is to reproduce the collision: merge, then
immediately dispatch with `publish_release` **off**, and confirm the dispatch
survives the merge's push run instead of being cancelled by it. That builds and
verifies without publishing anything.

body:
Thanks @yourspraveen for the report — it was precise enough to reproduce from the description alone.

**Problem.** When one self-hosted provider has several connections pointing at different hosts, each host keeps its own synced model inventory, but connection selection only consulted the manual `excludedModels` denylist — so a request could be routed to a host that never synced the model, surfacing as a spurious model-not-found.

**Fix.** Filter candidate connections by each connection's synced inventory, pinning the request to the host that actually advertises the model.

### Note on the path in the issue

The issue cites `src/lib/providerModels/syncedEndpointRouting.ts` as prior art. That file doesn't exist on this branch yet — it ships inside the still-open #11088, which is based on `main` and touches the images/embeddings paths. Building on it would not compile here.

So the logic went where the actual decision is made instead:

- `src/sse/services/auth.ts` — `loadAdvertisedModelsForSelfHostedConnections()`, one extra predicate in the candidate filter, and a `modelNotAdvertised` log branch alongside the existing `excluded` branch.
- `src/domain/connectionModelRules.ts` — `isModelAdvertisedByConnection()`, matching the same candidate semantics as the existing denylist helper.

It reuses `getSyncedAvailableModelsByConnection` (`src/lib/db/models.ts`), which already had five consumers; connection selection simply wasn't one of them.

**It fails open in three places** — empty inventory, malformed persisted row, or a DB read that throws all mean "unknown", never "this host lacks the model". A partial read must never silently shrink the connection pool. Scoped to `SELF_HOSTED_CHAT_PROVIDER_IDS`, so hosted providers don't pay an extra DB read.

### Evidence

**RED** — `src/` reverted to the parent commit, new test file kept:

```
tests 5 | pass 3 | fail 2
AssertionError: jetson never synced flux2-klein:9b and must not be selected for it
```

**GREEN** — with the fix: `tests 5 | pass 5 | fail 0`.

**Regression sweep** — 199 tests, 196 pass. The 3 failures (`session-affinity-generic-7274`, `provider-health-matrix`, a Codex virtual-children case) were each confirmed failing at unmodified `release/v3.8.50` too. Net: 0 regressions, +5 new passing tests.

Heads-up: `release/v3.8.50` is currently red for unrelated reasons (README migration counts, stale eslint suppressions, an incomplete Hack Club removal), so CI here may show pre-existing failures that this branch doesn't cause.

### Context

#11098 also nominally claims this issue. For maintainer awareness it is currently `CONFLICTING`, based on `main` rather than `release/v3.8.50`, and spans 3431 files / +583818 lines. Noting it only so the overlap isn't a surprise.

4 files, +287/-1. Rebased on `release/v3.8.50` @ `92ef3c71e`.

Closes #11089

body:
## What

Three related runtime-control fixes for the HERD-811 runtime-parity program (child HERD-830).

### 1. Model-switch routing (P3)
The coordinator step-up section now explicitly frames the mid-flight model step-up as driver-routed: the runtime's own `DRIVER_AGENT_MODEL_SWITCH` binding delivered through `DRIVER:send-text` (the existing `herd_driver_switch_model` helper, HERD-176 P4). Strengthened `test-watcher-driver-wake.sh` so codex/grok are proven to compose `/model <model>` **from their own binding** through the send-text seam — driver-neutral, not a claude hardcode.

### 2. Codex durable coordinator wired into the live path
`codex-durable-coordinator.sh` (HERD-766) had **zero live callers**. `herd-feature.sh` now routes a codex builder through it — a durable, steerable, resumable `codex exec resume` session instead of a one-shot TUI — when the ship-dormant `CODEX_DURABLE_LANE` lever is on **and** the resolved lane driver is codex. ## What was wrong
PR #1074 (this session, minutes earlier) referenced a bare `adopted` inside the `if (persistence) {...}` block in `sessionManager.js`'s `createSession()` — but `adopted` is a `const` scoped to the earlier `if (this.sessionPersistenceEnabled) {...}` block, out of scope by the time it's read again. Every session creation after a server restart threw `ReferenceError: adopted is not defined`, caught internally and logged, but the workspace UI was left with zero sessions and no visible error — looked exactly like "I lost all my worktrees."

Live-reproduced: after #1074 merged and the server restarted picking it up, a user with 5 open worktrees reconnected to find all of them gone. `logs/sessions.log` (not `combined.log` — session creation logs to its own file) showed the ReferenceError on every single adopted session.

Read `persistence.adopted` (already stored on the object one line above) instead of the out-of-scope bare `adopted`.

body:
## Summary

- `ExpenseForm` (a `Modal`-based Bottom Sheet since #50) rendered off-screen on real mobile devices — reported by the user with an actual iPhone screenshot showing only the dimmed backdrop, no visible panel. Automated tests passed because one specific scroll position happened to mask the bug.
- Root cause: `PullToRefresh.tsx` wraps `<main>` in a `<div>` carrying an unconditional `transform: translateY(0px)` at rest (needed for the rubber-band pull gesture). Per the CSS spec, *any* non-`none` `transform` on an ancestor — even a visually-inert zero translation — establishes a new containing block for `position: fixed` descendants. `Modal`'s `fixed inset-0` backdrop was therefore positioned relative to `PullToRefresh`'s wrapper box, which spans the entire scrollable page height (the expense list uses `react-virtuoso`'s `useWindowScroll`), not the actual viewport.
- Three CSS-only fixes to `PullToRefresh.tsx` itself were tried and rejected (see `docs/DECISIONS.md` for the full account): `transform: undefined` at rest (still left a `transition` targeting `transform` declared, which also triggers the containing-block rule), removing the whole inline style at rest, and switching to the standalone CSS `translate` property (which, per the modern spec, *also* establishes a containing block). None of these fixed the bug reliably, and two of them broke `react-virtuoso`'s list rendering on short pages.
- **The actual fix:** `Modal.tsx` now renders through `createPortal(..., document.body)`. A portaled node isn't a descendant of any ancestor's CSS for containing-block purposes — this is the standard fix for this bug class, and `PullToRefresh.tsx` is left completely unmodified.
- The portal change surfaced two more, smaller bugs that are also fixed here:
  - `react-virtuoso`'s `useWindowScroll` could measure a stale/zero window viewport on its first mount after a sequence of layout-affecting events (self-serve trip creation → admin panel → expense modal). Confirmed *not* a containing-block issue via live `offsetParent` DOM inspection. Fixed with an explicit `virtuosoRef.scrollTo()` nudge in `ExpensesPanel.tsx`.
  - `Modal` and `Toast` shared the identical `z-[9999]`. Portaling `Modal` moved it to the end of `document.body`'s DOM order, so a still-exit-animating delete-confirmation modal would silently cover and swallow clicks on the toast's "تراجع" (undo) button underneath. Fixed by bumping `Toast.tsx` to `z-[10000]`.

## Test plan

- [x] `e2e/expense-form-scroll-visibility.spec.ts` — two scenarios (open at page top, open after deep scroll) confirming the modal is always within the viewport; the top-of-page scenario specifically can't be accidentally masked the way the original single-scenario test was.
- [x] `e2e/delete-empty-trip.spec.ts`, `e2e/critical-flow.spec.ts`, `e2e/soft-delete-trash.spec.ts` — each re-run standalone multiple times (3-4x) to confirm reliability, not just a single pass.
- [x] Full `npm run test:e2e` suite green.
- [x] `npm run lint && npm run typecheck && npm test && npm run build` all clean.
- [x] Full investigation and rationale documented in `docs/DECISIONS.md`.

author: pjordanandrsn
body:
Five single-variable explanations for the frequency/recency split are now dead:

| candidate | verdict |
|---|---|
| popularity skew | refuted ([#189](https://github.com/pjordanandrsn/grouped-nf4-gemm/pull/189)) |
| working-set pressure | refuted |
| reuse distance | refuted |
| `k/E` | ruled out — OLMoE and gpt-oss share 0.125 at opposite ends |
| **top-k** | **refuted, preregistered** ([#192](https://github.com/pjordanandrsn/grouped-nf4-gemm/pull/192)) |

After five, the prior on a sixth is low — and this program has already recorded what fitting a rule to four points costs.

So the question changes: not *why* frequency helps on some models, but whether a policy can **avoid needing to know**. ARC arbitrates exactly the axis these models disagree on, it's online, and it's implementable — none of which is true of Belady.

## The predictions

- **A1** — per model, median `ARC ÷ min(LRU, LFU)` ≤ **1.02**. Adaptivity that loses to both alternatives it adapts between isn't worth shipping; 2% is the slack for not knowing in advance.
- **A2**, the one that matters — on **gpt-oss**, ARC closes **≥ 15%** of the LRU-to-Belady gap. LFU closes **2%** there. If ARC also closes ~2%, adaptivity buys nothing on the model every wall measurement was made on, and the idea is dead whatever it does elsewhere.

Registered explicitly: **A1 confirmed with A2 refuted is a negative outcome** — ARC safe but pointless, gap still open — not a partial win.

## Two preconditions on reporting anything

**Falsifiability.** Both predictions get the `structural_check.py` treatment — synthetic routing swept across stickiness and skew — to confirm the verdicts *can* move. This program has published a confirmation no input could have refuted; it won't do it twice. Anything forced is reported as uninformative.

**Implementation.** ARC is subtle enough to get wrong in ways that still produce plausible numbers, so it's validated before it's trusted:

- at capacity ≥ the whole key space, ARC / LRU / LFU / Belady must all agree — everything fits, so no policy can differ;
- ARC must never exceed the all-miss count nor fall below Belady;
- resident + ghost must never exceed `2c` — ARC's own invariant, and what a broken port violates silently.

A failure of any of these means the *implementation* is being scored, not the policy.

**LIRS, 2Q and tuned hybrids are out of scope by registration.** Trying several and reporting the winner is the failure mode this file exists to avoid.

No box needed — this is offline on traces already committed.

## Summary

Restarts `chatgpt-tool-shim` as an active project and implements the first working architecture slice across the ChatGPT adapter, result transport, localhost broker, milestones, and debug tooling.

### Architecture and project structure

- treats the extension as a thin ChatGPT-specific adapter
- keeps the localhost capability broker under `server/` during protocol iteration
- documents explicit criteria for splitting the broker into its own repository later
- adds canonical checkbox milestones M0–M6
- formalizes inline vs attachment result transport and call correlation

### ChatGPT adapter work

- hardens composer/send selectors around the active composer scope
- removes dangerously broad generic submit-button selection
- adds file-input discovery for result attachments
- adds structured selector/DOM diagnostics export
- adds a bounded call state trace
- adds `Attach Large Results` and `Configure Broker` controls
- preserves call IDs across local broker execution

### Attachment result transport

- routes small results inline
- packages large successful results into versioned JSON `File` attachments
- uses correlated filenames and `<tool_result_ref>` messages
- waits for a stable attachment-ready state before auto-submit
- returns compact delivery errors instead of dumping giant failed payloads inline
- adds unit coverage for packaging/filename/ref behavior

### Local capability broker MVP

- Node/TypeScript broker bundled with esbuild
- binds to `127.0.0.1` only
- bearer-token authentication
- ephemeral secure token generation when no token is configured
- `GET /health`
- authenticated `GET /v1/capabilities`
- authenticated `POST /v1/execute`
- compatibility `POST /tool`
- capability registry and normalized errors
- starter capabilities: `broker.hello`, `broker.clock`, `system.runtime`
- extension-side token and call-ID propagation

### Diagnostics

- adds `npm run debug:bundle`
- bundles git state, runtime versions, tests, build output, broker health, and explicitly supplied `debug-input/`
- overlay can download `extension-diagnostics-*.json`
- diagnostics deliberately omit broker tokens, page text, cookies, browser profile data, and arbitrary local files

## First local acceptance path

1. `npm install`
2. `npm test`
3. `npm run build`
4. load `dist/` unpacked in Edge
5. `npm run server:start`
6. copy the generated token into **Configure Broker**
7. test `local.mcp.call` -> `broker.hello`
8. test a large result / attachment path
9. click **Download Diagnostics**, place it in `debug-input/`, run `npm run debug:bundle`, and share the ZIP if anything fails

This remains a draft until the current ChatGPT DOM and upload path are verified in a real local browser session.

## What this PR does

When reasoning is disabled (`includeThoughts: false` on a request, e.g. the AUTO-mode classifier's stage-1 side query, or config-level `reasoning: false`) and the endpoint is OpenRouter (`openrouter.ai` or a subdomain), the OpenAI-compatible pipeline now emits OpenRouter's native thinking-disable parameter `reasoning: { enabled: false }` on the wire request. The detection is a hostname-only helper (`isOpenRouterHostname`) mirroring the existing `isDeepSeekHostname` precedent, and the emission sits in the `reasoningDisabled` branch after the unconditional `reasoning` / `reasoning_effort` strip, because the provider `buildRequest` hook runs before that strip and anything emitted there would be removed again.

## Why it's needed

Fixes the failure chain in #9757: the classifier's stage 1 is a structured side query that forces a `respond_in_schema` tool call (`tool_choice: 'required'`, forced-tool mapping from #6929) with a 256-token budget and `thinkingConfig: { includeThoughts: false }`. On OpenRouter the thinking-disable only rendered into shapes the gateway ignores — `chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking` (the vLLM/SGLang shape) for qwen-family models — and the pipeline then stripped the `reasoning` object, which is exactly OpenRouter's native thinking knob. Thinking stayed enabled, the model spent the whole 256-token budget on reasoning and never emitted the forced tool call, `generateJson` returned `{}`, schema validation failed, and the classifier fail-closed with `Classifier stage 1 unavailable`, forcing manual approval for every AUTO-mode action. This is a residual gap next to #6929 (which added the forced tool call + budget), not a duplicate: #6929 works wherever the thinking-disable actually lands, but OpenRouter was missing from the disable-rendering logic. It is also disjoint from #9590 (still open), which covers DeepSeek/GLM/Kimi thinking controls on the WebShell UI and does not touch the OpenRouter classifier path.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Detector-level reproduction and regression coverage live in `packages/core/src/core/openaiContentGenerator/pipeline.test.ts` (search `OpenRouter`): with `baseUrl: https://openrouter.ai/api/v1` and `thinkingConfig: { includeThoughts: false }`, the captured `chat.completions.create` body is asserted to carry `reasoning: { enabled: false }`. On unpatched main these tests fail with `reasoning: undefined`; with this PR they pass. Negative guards: no `reasoning` field leaks to the official OpenAI endpoint, to non-OpenRouter OpenAI-compatible gateways (vLLM/SGLang), or to lookalike hostnames (`openrouter.ai.evil.com`), and `thinkingMandatory` models on OpenRouter stay exempt. - Main risk or tradeoff: `reasoning: { enabled: false }` is now sent on every reasoning-disabled request to OpenRouter hostnames regardless of model family. That is intentional — `reasoning` is an OpenRouter provider-level parameter the gateway routes to whatever model supports it (unlike `enable_thinking`, a qwen-specific wire field that the existing code deliberately family-gates to avoid leaking upstream) — but it means OpenRouter-side handling of the parameter is the only validation so far.

body:
Reported: *"I asked you for your two highest-conviction picks — NVDA and SpaceX — and in all the boards you have built me those have never come up. There has to be a better board than all the ones we have built."*

## The complaint was correct, and it is not a bug in any single board

Every live ranking board looks for a **dislocation**:

| board | ranks |
|---|---|
| quiet-strength | the part of a 12-1 move factor exposure does *not* explain |
| insider | open-market buying by people with non-public information |
| catalyst | an identifiable near-term event |
| earnings | a surprise against consensus |
| crosses | a technical regime change |

A dislocation screen is by construction a **non-consensus** screen, so the most consensus large-cap on earth cannot rank on any of them. Quiet Strength is the sharpest case: it regresses the move onto the factors and ranks the **residual**, so a mega-cap whose move is factor-explained scores near zero *by design*. Nothing we owned looked for a durable franchise compounding at a high rate.

(SpaceX is a separate matter — it is private, so no equity screen can ever return it.)

## Quiet Strength is not broken, either

Checked against production while diagnosing this: snapshot 20.3h old, `stale:false`, health green, 1,638 of 1,854 scored. What is frozen is the *input* — `factorLatestYm` and `scoringEndYm` are both **202606**, so every nightly re-run re-scores an identical window. The board cannot move until July factors land. Worth surfacing a formation date on that view separately; it is not part of this PR.

## The design, and what it is measured on

Built to the two survivors in `reports/research-2026-08/screener-evidence.md`, the review commissioned after all seven boards were measured and none beat buy-and-hold:

- **Momentum 12-1 with the one-month skip** — best-replicated anomaly, best HXZ survivor.
- **Profitability** — survives HXZ *and* the q-factor model; QMJ positive in 23 of 24 countries.
- **Integrated** scoring (Fisher/Shah/Titman), not two sleeves.

Blend is quality-led 0.6 / 0.4, with a bottom-quartile quality floor against junk momentum, and no name ranked on half the evidence.

### Three departures, all stated in the code rather than left to be noticed

1. **No value axis.** The house recommendation is integrated quality-*value*. A cheapness axis is precisely what excludes a 33x-earnings franchise. Permitted by the same report's finding that splitting a momentum portfolio by value does not add — but it is a departure and is labelled one.
2. **Gross profitability, not cash-based.** The report's survivor is *cash-based* operating profitability and calls the definition load-bearing. We ship Novy-Marx gross profits/assets because `gross_profit` and `total_assets` are what the provider returns. That is a real weakening of the evidence behind the axis.
3. **A quality floor with no reciprocal momentum floor** — an asymmetry that favours the profile that prompted the board.

### What I did not do

Measured from live data: NVDA's gross profits/assets is **~0.64** against a top-quintile threshold near 0.33–0.40, but its trailing-year relative strength vs SPY is **+2.23%** and it sits at the 69.9th percentile of its own 52-week range. It is a quality outlier that is **not** a momentum leader — so I did not build the momentum board I first assumed would fix this, and I did not tune weights to lift it further. Verdict ships **UNMEASURED**, and a forward-league cohort is registered so it can actually earn a t-statistic.

## Defects found by the two review passes, including two in my own core

**Ship-blockers**
- **No `netlify.toml` redirect.** `/api/compounders-board` fell through to the SPA catch-all and returned `index.html` with status 200 — the endpoint would have looked wired and served garbage. Not one line of this board was reachable in production.
- **A provider outage could overwrite a good board with an empty one.** `fetchFinvizScreener` returns null rather than throwing, `universeChecked` was set to the *finalist* count, and every arm of `assessSnapshotPublish` is denominator-gated — so a total universe failure arrived as 0 and missed all of them. Now: universe-based denominator, partial-universe detection (one index leg missing), and a worker floor.
- **Cron collided exactly with `scan-insider-ndx`** at 21:40. `DAILY_CLOSE_SLOTS` registers the insider family at its earliest slot only, which is what hid it. Moved to 21:55.

**Correctness**
- **The window and the maths disagreed.** `momentumWindow` chose anchors t-12 and t-2 while `trailingReturnPct` derived its own start as `endYm - MOMENTUM_MONTHS`, asking for a month never fetched — every name scored momentum null and the board came back empty *with no warning*. Span now derives from the window object. The window was also 12 returns where the house 12-1 is 11 (t-12..t-2), so two boards printed the same column label over different windows.
- **Quality percentiles were pooled across bases** (mine). `qualityOf` returns a ratio (~0.1–0.7) for exact and a percent (~5–40) for the ROE fallback — pooled, a few failed statement fetches put proxied names at the top on units alone, looking entirely normal. Ranked within basis now.
- **The ROE fallback was stamped `roic-proxy`** (mine). ROE is leverage-inflatable, ROIC is not. Added a truthful `roe-proxy` token.
- Dropped a duplicate `rows` array that escaped the 1 MiB trim; registered the board in `snapshot-history` `VALID_BOARDS` (omitting it 400s every History request — the screens rollout already shipped that bug) and in `FORWARD_BOARDS`.

**Honesty**
- The first commit claimed the weights "were not tuned to place any particular ticker." A review measured that the test suite pinned an NVDA-shaped placement tightly enough to **lock `QUALITY_WEIGHT` at ≥ ~0.57**. Nobody swept a parameter, but a ticker-shaped result had become a regression invariant. Those assertions now test the mechanism. **Verified after the rewrite:** the suite passes at 0.55, 0.60, 0.75 and 0.80; the only failing value is 0.50, and it fails on "leads with quality" — the stated design.

## Verification

- `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean
- `npx vitest run` — **3191 of 3192 pass**. The one failure (`provider-transport-null` → `getInsiderActivity`) reproduces on a clean `git stash` of HEAD and is unrelated.
- `npm run build` — clean

`APP_VERSION` 0.79.2-alpha → 0.80.0-alpha.

## Note on the branch

#208 was squash-merged, so this branch was restarted from `main` and force-pushed over history already contained in `main` (verified: the only tree difference was later automated paper-track commits). No unmerged work was discarded.

## Why

`has_resource`, `intel_level` and `is_war_participant` are each declared as one scalar form and one block form. The trigger emitter only accepted that overload when the scalar was a localisation key, because `typeof value === "string"` was its only runtime discriminator.

## What

- The shared `scalarOrFields` shape carries the scalar arm's `TsValue`; the emitted builder dispatches with `isStructuredValue(value, <objectKinds>)`, the same discriminator the nested-field model and the effect recorder already use. A plain object is the block; an SDK ref object is the scalar only when the rules admit that ref kind.
- The scalar arm records a content reference exactly like a whole-value trigger (`scalarEntryReturn`, shared with `emitValue`).
- Generated `*Args` of overloaded triggers are now type aliases: an interface has no implicit index signature, so TypeScript would keep it in both branches of the narrowing and neither arm would typecheck without a cast.
- Three `SDK-248` ledger rows deleted (41 → 38).

Emitted: `hasResource(value: ResourceRef | string | boolean)` / `hasResource(args: { type; amount })`, `intelLevel(value: IntelLevel)` / `intelLevel(args: { level; system })`, `isWarParticipant(value: ScopeValue<...>)` / `isWarParticipant(args: { who?; war?; side? })`.

## Noted

Vanilla writes `intel_level = { level > none ... }` while `triggers.cwt:1587` declares `level = enum[intel_level]`. Left as declared; that is a rules fix for the fork.

## Verification

`npm run codegen`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm test` (3221 tests), `npm run build`, `npm run codegen:check` — all pass. Render goldens for both arms of each trigger; type tests reject a block missing `amount`, a non-string selector, and a wrong-typed scalar.

body:
## Problema

`ios-build.yml` roda em `macos-latest` (10x o custo de minutos do GitHub Actions vs Linux) e, junto com `android-build.yml`, disparava automaticamente em todo push para `main`. Hoje (2026-08-22) houve ~50 pushes/merges para `main`, cada um disparando build iOS + Android + os outros workflows (CI, Playwright, SonarQube, Quality).

A partir de ~21:09 de hoje, todos os checks de CI em PRs abertos começaram a falhar em segundos com a anotação `The job was not started because your account is locked due to a billing issue.` — consistente com a cota de minutos gratuitos do plano tendo estourado, provavelmente puxada pelos builds iOS repetidos.

## Correção

Remove o gatilho `push: branches: [main]` de `ios-build.yml` e `android-build.yml`, deixando só `workflow_dispatch`. Os builds mobile passam a rodar apenas quando alguém decidir gerar um build de verdade, não a cada merge.

## O que isso não resolve

Não desfaz os minutos já consumidos hoje — só estanca o consumo daqui pra frente. A cota deve resetar no próximo ciclo de faturamento da conta.

## Test plan

- [ ] Confirmar que `ios-build.yml`/`android-build.yml` não disparam mais em push para `main` após o merge
- [ ] Disparar manualmente (`workflow_dispatch`) uma vez para confirmar que o build ainda funciona quando necessário

author: antigerme
body:
O @antigerme viu as requisições ao Cloudflare crescerem muito. A causa é minha, e é **uma linha**.

## O bug

`ws.onopen` zerava `Presenca.tentativa`. Mas **abrir o socket não é ter conectado**: a recusa do crachá, o fechamento pelo servidor e a queda de rede vêm todos *depois* do `onopen`. Zerando ali, o contador volta a zero a cada tentativa e o recuo usa pra sempre o primeiro degrau.

## Medido

Servidor aceitando o upgrade e fechando logo depois:

```
antes:   16 tentativas em 31s — esperas 2 · 2 · 2 · 2 · 2 · 2 · 2 · 2 · 2 …
depois:  esperas 1,7 · 6 · 12,5 · … até o teto de 60s
```

Cada tentativa custa **duas** requisições ao Worker (o `/api/presenca` do crachá e o upgrade do WebSocket) e **uma** chamada ao `/Session` do Waze.

| | tentativas/hora | requisições ao Worker/hora |
|---|---|---|
| antes | ~1.800 | **~3.600** |
| depois | ~60 | **~120** |

**30× menos.** E não é só cota da Cloudflare: era dado do celular do editor, torrado em silêncio.

## O conserto

Quem zera o recuo agora é a mensagem **`eu`**, que só chega se o servidor conferiu o crachá e aceitou. É a única prova de que a conexão serve pra alguma coisa.

Junto vai **jitter de ±25%** na espera, pelo mesmo motivo que o projeto já exige jitter nas chamadas ao Waze — agora do lado do cliente. Servidor que cai desconecta todo mundo no mesmo instante; espera igual pra todos transforma uma queda numa rajada sincronizada de volta.

## Guards

Dois, conferidos rodando com o código que estava em produção — reprovam:

- o `onopen` não pode zerar o recuo
- a espera de reconexão não pode ser fixa

## Nota

Este é o tipo de bug que nenhum dos meus testes pegaria: o smoke exercita o caminho **feliz** (conecta, conversa, sai) e os testes de protocolo exercitam o **servidor**. A política de reconexão do cliente só aparece quando algo falha *repetidamente* — e nada media isso. Agora mede.

243 testes verdes. Serial `v2026.08.23-01` (o `date -u` virou o dia no meio do trabalho, então a revisão zera).

author: baron-3dl
body:
## What

LINK.EXE's EVAX/Alpha path now emits a `.vms$rel` load-bias fixup table so a real GCC-port program's global initialized pointers survive a non-zero IMGACT load bias. Before this fix the EVAX path wrote image-relative pointers as unbiased absolutes (correct only at load-bias 0); a `const char *g_ptr = greeting;` (a REFQUAD in `$DATA$`) held `greeting`'s unbiased offset, so under bias B it pointed at `off` instead of `B+off`.

## The fix

Records, in the existing `OVMX_REL` format (`ovmx_image.h`: magic `REL1`, `ovmx_rel_header` + u64 offsets), every EVAX slot LINK fills with an unbiased image-relative address:
- **REFQUAD / CODEADDR** to a section-relative (`to_section >= 0`) or local-defined target
- **LINKAGE** local pair — both quads (code entry + descriptor)

IMGACT's generic `apply_vms_rel` (imgact.c) adds the load bias at activation — no IMGACT change; the same table + contract the ELF `emit_shareable` path already emits.

**Excluded** (mirrors the ELF policy): folded globalvalues (absolute link-time constants, resolve through an unplaced `$ABS$` section → `sec_base == 0`) and cross-image `.vms$imp` imports (IMGACT fills those; biasing would double-count).

**REFLONG:** the alpha-dec-vms port emits no REFLONG to a placed section (all runtime pointers/addresses are REFQUAD/CODEADDR/LINKAGE quads; the only REFLONGs are `$ABS$`/globalvalue folds). A 4-byte slot can't hold a 64-bit-biased address, so a REFLONG-to-placed-section fails honestly (unreachable with the current port; kept as the honest guard).

## Test (verify-first: emit AND consume)

`run_evax_vmsrel.sh` + `evax_vmsrel_verify.c`, wired into `ci.yml`:
- **PART A** links `gdata.obj`, asserts the `g_ptr` slot is in `.vms$rel` (magic REL1, count 3), then replicates IMGACT `apply_vms_rel`'s exact `*(base+off)+=base` walk at bias `B=0x40000000` and asserts `g_ptr` resolves to `B+greeting_off` (before: `greeting_off`; after: `B+greeting_off`).
- **PART B** a folded GLOBALVALUE (`.quad C$_EXIT1`) yields NO `.vms$rel` entry.
- **PART C** cross-image `.vms$imp` import patch_off slots are excluded while the section-relative slot is recorded.

Joint crt0+app EVAX link stays clean: 6 correct fixups recorded, 5 `decc$` imports excluded, zero deferred. EVAX regressions (read/link/ximport/gvalfold) green.

author: goldenphysicsproject
body:
## Summary

Corrects a wrong central finding from the previous merged round (PR #114) and lands the correct result rigorously in Lean.

**The error**: PR #114's "central finding" tested whether the Fourier-coefficient sequence of `K_p - 1` (indices = frequencies) is itself positive-definite as a Toeplitz kernel — found indefinite, reported as "no positivity-preserving projection exists." That answers the wrong question. The question that matters for kernel positivity is whether the Gram matrix `M_{jk} = (K_p-1)(θ_j-θ_k)` (indices = point evaluations at arbitrary finite angle configurations) is positive semidefinite.

**Corrected finding, proved rigorously**: `K_p − 1` **is** a positive kernel, prime-by-prime, unconditionally — trivially, since convolution by `K_p` is diagonal in the Fourier basis with nonnegative eigenvalues `r^{|n|}`, and the vacuum subtraction only zeroes the `n=0` eigenvalue (which can't make the rest negative).

## Layered proof development

A first attempt at the corrected result proved the untruncated two-sided `HasSum` over all of `ℤ` and built `PositiveType(K_r-1)` on top of it as one monolithic theorem. Both repeatedly hit `(deterministic) timeout at whnf` — even at 4,000,000 heartbeats (20× default). Bisected via standalone scratch-file tests at *default* heartbeats (seconds, not minutes, per test) to two root causes: `HasSum.of_nat_of_neg_add_one` elaborating cheaply alone but expensively in a large local context, and the full Gram-square argument accumulating unbounded `ring_nf`/`nlinarith` cost over an infinite series inside one proof.

Fixed architecturally (per review), not by raising heartbeats further — restructured into four small, independently-fast layers (each builds in **under 4 seconds standalone**):

- `gram_square_freq` — fixed-frequency Gram identity (generalizes the pre-existing `gram_square_nonneg` from `ConvolutionSquarePositive.lean` to complex amplitudes)
- `gram_square_freqSum` — finite weighted sum over frequencies
- `gram_square_freqSum_nonneg` — nonnegativity corollary
- `KrN0` / `KrN0_gram_nonneg` — the truncated kernel `K⁰_{r,N}=Σ_{0<|n|≤N}r^{|n|}e^{inθ}` and the milestone: `Σⱼₖ c̄ⱼcₖK⁰_{r,N}(xⱼ-xₖ)≥0` for every truncation `N`.

## Honest boundary (unchanged in substance)

Deferred, not attempted: the untruncated `HasSum` over all of `ℤ`, the `N→∞` limit passage, the `H(t)` Fourier-pair/pole-cancellation proofs (still numerical-only), and the Hilbert-space operator identity `P_0·C_K·P_0 = C_{K-1} = (A·P_0)*(A·P_0)`. This correction does **not** establish global Weil positivity — single-prime kernel positivity was never going to answer that on its own. No RH claim, no Connes–Consani machinery imported.

## Test plan

- [x] `lake build GppVerify.RiemannHypothesis.CutkoskyWeilBridge` — clean, fast.
- [x] `lake build GppVerify` (full project) — clean.
- [x] `lake env lean scripts/check_axioms.lean` — all 7 theorems in this file (`Kp_pos`, `H_nonneg`, `Kp_eq_KrClosed`, `gram_square_freq`, `gram_square_freqSum`, `gram_square_freqSum_nonneg`, `KrN0_gram_nonneg`) depend only on Lean built-ins.
- [x] `python3 discovery/cutkosky_weil/cutkosky_weil_verify.py` — corrected Gram-matrix positivity confirmed numerically for random non-equally-spaced point configurations, `p=2,3,5`.
- [ ] CI (`build.yml`, `blueprint.yml`) — to be verified green on this PR before merge.

author: bigredprof
body:
The mirror of #57, found by the digihouse migration.

`PackDatum<M>` went through the strongly typed pack, so a caller holding a model as `object` — the ordinary case when packing whatever arrived — inferred `M = object` and needed a `PackRat<object>` that cannot exist.

Digihouse hit it in three places on the first run, all with the same signature shape:

```csharp
public string ConstructMessage(MessageSource source, MessageType type, object model, string schemaId)
{
    Datum datum = PiedPiper.PackDatum(model, schemaId);   // throws
```

`EnvelopeHelper.CreateEnvelope` and `GatehouseClient.RecordModelAsync` take `object model` too, so the same failure was latent in both.

#57 fixed exactly this on the read side: `Datum.Unpack<M>` unpacks weakly and coerces, because the model type is the caller's question rather than the datum's. The write side needed the same and did not get it — I fixed the half the stories migration exercised and left the half it did not.

`PackDatum` now packs through the weakly typed path, which dispatches on the runtime type via the registered pack rat, so naming the type is optional in both directions. A null guard comes with it, since the weakly typed overload takes a non-nullable `object`.

Test covers the case digihouse hit: a model held as `object`, packed and read back.

`task verify` green: 525 tests.

author: mindsers
body:
## Description

Two related fixes: the first closes an access-control hole, the second stops sending
people to a page their assignment is not on.

### Section visibility in the viewers

Section visibility is an access-control rule with no manager bypass — the board listing
and the dashboard both apply it. Four routes that load a resource by id did not:

| Route | Guard before |
|---|---|
| `dynamic/viewer.tsx` | `BoardViewer` only |
| `documents/viewer.tsx` | `BoardViewer` only |
| `documents/pdf-loader.tsx` (the file itself) | `BoardViewer` only |
| `documents/thumbnail.tsx` | **none at all** |

So anyone holding `BoardViewer` could read a restricted section's documents — and their
bytes — by walking ids. The notification links we send point at the first of those.

Each now loads *through* the filter rather than checking afterwards, so "you may not see
this" and "there is no such row" become the same answer. The rule is extracted into
`buildSectionVisibilityFilter`, and the two copies that already existed now call it:
three copies of an access-control predicate is how they drift apart.

### Programme link resolution

`resolveProgrammeLink` matched a document on template alone. A document only renders
released events from the start of the current month onwards, so a draft assignment — or
one that had aged out — resolved to a programme it was not in. And
`filterDynamicDataToEvent` silently fell back to rendering everything, leaving the reader
to search a list for something that isn't there.

The link now confirms the document can actually hold the event, and falls back to
`/board` when none can.

Where several documents hold it, the narrowest config wins and id breaks the tie, so the
same event always resolves the same way. Nothing in the model says which document an
event belongs to — giving a document a scope of its own is what would answer that
properly.

### Sharing an unreleased programme

The share button offered a message for any part the viewer could edit, including on a
draft. Since a document only renders released events, that link resolves to `/board` and
the reader is left with nothing — and the assignment may still change before it is
published. The notification path already stays quiet on drafts for the same reason, so
the rule belongs with the message building rather than in the route:
`buildShareTextsForEvent` returns nothing for an unreleased programme, and does not even
resolve a link for one.

### Saying when a document has no such event

`filterDynamicDataToEvent` now reports the miss alongside the data — the full programme
is still better than a blank page — and the viewer says so instead of leaving the reader
to hunt a list for something that isn't in it.

New key `board_viewer_event_not_here` added to `fr.json` **and** `en.json`.

## Type de changement

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] Refactoring (pas de changement fonctionnel)

## Checklist

- [x] J'ai formaté mon code avant de pousser (`pnpm build:format`)
- [x] J'ai mis à jour la documentation si nécessaire

## Verification

2966 unit tests · 317 integration tests · typecheck · lint · all six architecture guards.

The integration fixtures used fixed July dates that had already fallen outside the
window; they are now relative and cannot rot the same way again.
